cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Hand Over the Proof
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender information, evidence, a key, or access that would let you proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll arrange the visit to Dad. Give me the note you're using to say I can't come.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can read it to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can read it first. I still need to see the words before I book anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fold the rest under. Show me the line about visiting; I'll respect what it says.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads arranging Dad visit and asks for controlling evidence; A3 permits B reading first but needs direct words; A5 narrows access and promises respect for the line to keep B cooperating.

responseLogic.evidence: A1 note is used to bar A visit; B4 privacy supports folding other content away; no full permission to visit is assumed before the note is seen.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers oral reading and B4 protects private contents, giving A real terms to negotiate.

heightening.evidence: B4 privacy causes A5 selective exposure rather than the full-note demand, with a practical promise about using it.

specificity.evidence: A1 visit to Dad and exclusion based on a note establish why access matters before booking.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 folding, relevant-line request and respecting its terms all contribute to obtaining limited access.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 offers a substitute for direct access requested in A1.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 gives the privacy limit behind resisting A3.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 accommodates B4 by narrowing visible information and how A will act on it.
